name: Bellingshausen and Lazarev round Antarctica
traveler: Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen and Mikhail Lazarev
summary: Two Russian sloops, the Vostok and the Mirny, sail round the world in the far south to finish what Cook began. On 28 January 1820 they see a wall of ice stretching to the horizon off what is now Dronning Maud Land: the first sighting of the Antarctic continent, three days before Bransfield sights the peninsula. A year later they find Peter I Island and the coast of Alexander I Land.

stops.note: The Vostok and the Mirny sail in July.
Across the Atlantic to the last port before the south.
They chart its southern coast, which Cook had left unfinished.
The chain is charted and found to be islands, not a cape of a southern land.
A solid wall of ice, rising towards the south: the first sight of the Antarctic continent.
Along the edge of the pack ice to Sydney for the southern winter.
A winter cruise among the Tuamotus, where they chart new islands, and Tahiti.
The southernmost land yet found, named for the founder of the Russian navy.
Mountains behind the ice, which they take for a coast.
They meet the American sealer Nathaniel Palmer among the islands.
Home after 751 days, having circled the continent without being sure they had seen it.
